In 1325, two Italian cities went to war over a wooden bucket!
Two thousand men died. And the bucket? It never went back.
It started with Bologna and Modena, two rival cities, who hated each other.
One night, Modenese soldiers sneaked into Bologna, and stole a bucket from a public well.
Not gold. Not a crown. A bucket.
Bologna demanded it back. Modena said no. So Bologna raised an army of thirty thousand men, and marched out to get it.
Modena had only a fraction of that. But their knights charged first, and the Bolognese army collapsed.
They ran, and Modena's riders chased them all the way to the gates of Bologna.
Bologna lost the battle, and the bucket.
Today, that bucket is still in Modena, and Bologna is still waiting.
A poet even wrote a famous comic epic about it, called, The Stolen Bucket.
